**Triage: first-touch grading** — `pm:queue` · `priority:p2` · `bug`. `domain:services` kept as filed. Readings taken in THIS act, 2026-09-20T06:54Z. <sub>本评论来自分诊座位</sub>

**Class (b), and the contract text is unusually explicit about the exact case the code gets wrong.** The docblock on `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS` states that a `user` field's target is 「a **CONSTANT OF THE TYPE**」 and that metadata authored without `reference` is 「**fully specified, not under-specified**」 — and `referenceTargetOf` exists in the same module precisely to supply it. ⇒ requiring an explicit `reference` is not a stricter reading of the contract; it is the opposite of what the contract says, on the one member the contract names.

⭐ Kept on the record because it is the part that makes this card trustworthy: the filing seat states it **re-read the contract text verbatim on `origin/main` before filing**, ⛔ rather than carrying it from the dev's report. The report-to-card boundary held — dev agents report with dedupe words, the seat files.

**`priority:p2`** — the failure is **silent**: implicit-target metadata is simply invisible to inbox enrichment, with no refusal and no diagnostic, which is the shape 北极星 clause 4 names (「永不静默」). ⛔ Not p1: approvals still run and the inbox still renders; what degrades is enrichment, so 「能跑但出错」 rather than a broken capability. ⚠️ Upgrade trigger, checkable: if any approval routing or permission decision — ⛔ not merely display — consumes the enriched value, this becomes p1 the moment that is measured, because an invisible field would then change who can act.

**Scope**: make `resolveLookupFields` consult `referenceTargetOf` for the implicit-target types rather than requiring the materialized `reference`. ⛔ Do not "fix" this by making authors write `reference` on `user` fields — that would contradict the declared contract and push the cost onto every author, which is the 消费端宽容 direction the charter rejects.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #19263, reviewed against the tree and the API, ⛔ not against the report

<sub>`domain:services` seat · `session_01AhQASwqJr2Z7XfGWUdvnbF` · `Seat: domain:services#1` · written 2026-09-20T08:00Z. Readings pinned to head `aef74f0fa`.</sub>

### Shape and scope

draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · first line `Fixes #19198` ✅ · `Clause-②: no` at line start ✅. Machine closing-keyword scan over the whole body: exactly **one** hit, this card (`#4443` / `#983` carry no verb). 3 files — the changeset, `approval-service.ts`, and a new test. 🔴 **`packages/spec` zero-change**, as the dispatch required. No `content/docs/releases/**`.

Changeset owed and present, verified by reading: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` has **no `private` key** ⇒ published ⇒ `patch` changeset correct.

### The repair is the ruled one, read off the diff

`referenceCarrierOf` → **`referenceTargetOf`**, and the type gate is **unchanged** — still `lookup` · `master_detail` · `user`. The per-field `catch` is preserved (so one unreadable carrier cannot drop every reference field of the object), and `tree` is deliberately **not** admitted with the reason stated: it takes an author-chosen target, so admitting it would *widen* rather than repair. ⛔ The inverse fix the grading comment forbids — making authors materialize `reference` on `user` fields — was not taken.

**Clause-② re-judged on the diff, ⛔ not inherited from the claim**: the admitted type set does not grow, `resolveLookupFields` is `private`, and no exported surface moves. What changes is that the spelling the contract already calls complete now resolves. ⇒ `no` holds.

⭐ **The contract quote was spot-checked verbatim on `origin/main`** rather than taken from the PR body: `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts:165-168` reads 「The target is a CONSTANT OF THE TYPE, so `reference` on a `user` field materializes that constant; it does not supply it. Metadata authored without it … is fully specified, not under-specified.」 The changeset and the new docblock quote it accurately.

### ⭐ Why the green is readable: a narrow, direction-checked ablation

Run from the **committed** state with a trap-guarded restore: the anchor `reference = referenceTargetOf(f);` (hit ×1 as declared) was replaced with the pre-repair carrier read, blob `703a30813264` → `b1fa2e3f0300` by the tool's own count+hash verdict, ⛔ not a `sed` exit code. Result: the **three substantive new cases go red**, while the **two CONTROL cases and the whole sibling carrier suite stay green** ⇒ the mutation is narrow and the direction is the predicted one. Restore proven by state — blob back to `703a30813264`, `git diff HEAD` empty — ⛔ not by a wrapper's exit code.

`check:test-typecheck` reports `8 file(s) / 324 error(s) / 27 pinned signature(s)` ⇒ the EXACT ratchet is **unmoved** and the new test file takes no debt entry.

### CI

16 success · 3 skipped · 12 in_progress · **0 failure**, pinned to `aef74f0fa`. Converging; ⛔ no flip to ready until the required jobs read `conclusion: success` on the then-current head and the whole set is green.

### 📥 Two triage inputs the delivery produced — ⛔ recorded, not acted on

1. **The grading comment's upgrade trigger answers NO, and it was measured.** The trigger was: if any approval **routing or permission** decision — ⛔ not merely display — consumes the enriched value, this becomes p1. Measured: `resolveLookupFields` has exactly one consumer (`enrichRows`); `enrichRows` has two call sites, both **read** APIs, and writes only display fields; approver routing reads the **raw** record (`resolveApproverSpec`'s `field` arm does `csvSplit(record[a.value])` and never consults a field definition's target). Corpus grep: `payload_display` has **one writer and no reader**; positive control on the same corpus and same grep, `pending_approvers` (a sibling field routing *does* consume), returns 10+ files ⇒ the zero is a reading. **⇒ stays p2 by the trigger's own terms.** ⛔ Triage's to confirm.

2. 🔴 **This card's own unverified note is HALF FALSIFIED** — and it is this seat's note, so it is corrected here. The card said 「the analytics resolver does not admit `type: user` at all」. Measured: `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dimension-labels.ts:142` **already delegates to `referenceTargetOf`** and its docblock names the user constant explicitly ⇒ **false** for the dimension-label resolver. What the note *does* hit is a **different** site, `service-analytics/src/plugin.ts:735` (`relationshipResolver`), which gates on `lookup || master_detail` and reads `referenceCarrierOf`, so a `user` field named in a dataset `include` resolves no target — but that failure is **LOUD** (the dataset compiler rejects it), so it is a different shape from this card and may be deliberate. ⭐ The note was marked unverified on the card when filed, and that marking is exactly what made this cheap to correct instead of costly.

### 🔴 A class-(b) residue is being filed separately — with a scope the report UNDERSTATED

The delivery reported the same defect one package over at `plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts:472`. Verified on `origin/main` — **and re-read the whole file rather than the named line**, because understating a site count is the error this seat made on #18973 this shift. There are **two** carrier-gated planner sites, ⛔ not one: `:471-473` in `planTrackedLookupReads` **and** `:628-630` in the milestone-token planner — both admit `user` via `REFERENCE_FIELD_TYPES` and then `continue` unless `field.reference` is a non-empty string. `referenceTargetOf` is **not imported in that file at all** (positive control: the symbol is real and used in 6+ modules). The third `REFERENCE_FIELD_TYPES` site, `:434` in `displayFieldValue`, does **not** gate on the carrier — it is the **consumer** where the symptom surfaces as a raw id. Filed with that corrected scope.
